version.changelog:
- Added platform compatibility notes for macOS (Docker Desktop) and Linux (Docker Engine).
- Specified required commands and clarified the Docker build/setup process.
- Updated seccomp profile to use a block-list approach for improved cross-platform support.
- Documented the official Docker image and its contents.
- Minor clarifications and enhanced setup instructions in SKILL.md.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (pre-install sandboxing) matches most of its code, but there are packaging/instruction inconsistencies and some missing files that make it unclear and worth manual inspection before use.

dimensions.detail: The code and instructions implement a 5-layer sandboxing protocol that legitimately requires Python and Docker and (optionally) Firecracker; these capabilities align with the description. However, the registry metadata claims 'required binaries: none' while SKILL.md lists docker and python3, which is an inconsistency in metadata vs runtime instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs building a Docker image 'from bundled Dockerfile' and running the orchestrator against arbitrary feature source directories. The manifest provided to the scanner does not show a Dockerfile in the file list (manifest omits a Dockerfile), and multiple files were truncated/omitted from the report (including microvm_orchestrator contents). That missing/contradictory packaging makes it unclear exactly what will be built/run. The scripts explicitly read arbitrary source directories and run/observe untrusted code inside containers/VMs — expected for a sandbox but worth attention because the missing files may contain additional behaviors.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only + bundled scripts). That is lower risk than pulling remote code during install. All code appears bundled in the skill package (no external downloads referenced in the visible files).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables and the visible scripts do not request credentials. The only runtime requirements are Docker and Python as stated in SKILL.md, which are proportionate to the sandboxing purpose. The optional Firecracker mode legitimately requires root/kernel access but is explicitly described as optional.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal autonomous invocation behavior. The skill does not request forced presence. However, the optional Firecracker micro-VM mode requires root privileges on the host — if the user runs that mode it increases risk; the orchestrator also relies on building/running a Docker image locally, which will create local artifacts. No evidence the skill changes other skills or global agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package appears to implement the sandboxing protocol it promises, but there are important packaging and visibility gaps you should resolve before installing or running it on any sensitive host:

- Confirm the Dockerfile: SKILL.md says the image is built from a bundled Dockerfile, but the provided manifest did not list a Dockerfile. Don’t run docker build until you verify the Dockerfile contents.

- Inspect omitted/truncated files: The microvm_orchestrator and a few other files were truncated/omitted in the scan. Review the full contents of microvm_orchestrator.py, any Dockerfile, and any other omitted files for hidden network calls, URL downloads, or commands executed with elevated privileges.

- Run in a disposable environment first: Execute the skill on an isolated machine or VM that you can destroy (not your production host). Prefer Docker mode (non-root) and avoid Firecracker/root mode unless you trust the code after review.

- Verify seccomp and no-network guarantees: Inspect scripts/seccomp-profile.json and microvm_orchestrator to confirm network syscalls and other sensitive syscalls are blocked as claimed.

- Check artifact handling: The tool reads arbitrary source dirs and writes outputs; ensure you point it at copies of code (not your real production configs) and that it does not unintentionally modify source files.

If you provide the missing Dockerfile and the full microvm_orchestrator.py (and any other omitted files), I can re-evaluate — that information would likely raise my confidence to 'high' for a benign verdict if the files match the documented behavior.
